title: Private control plane — evacuation, scalability & Terraform notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, hands-on runbook for private control-plane deployments (VPC and on-prem variants). Focus: initial setup sanity checks, safe scaling patterns, rapid evacuation/maintenance procedures, and Terraform module notes that reduce upgrade risk. This doc is intentionally operational — short commands, checklists, and known gotchas for on-call and SREs preparing customer rollouts.

Scope / audience:
- Eng-private-deployments and SRE on-call.
- Field engineers doing customer installs.
- Release engineers preparing control-plane upgrades.

Assumptions & environment patterns:
- Control plane runs in customer-managed VPC or air-gapped datacenter.
- Infra provisioned by terraform-modules repo (see linked PR).
- State is stored remotely (GCS bucket or S3) and encrypted with customer KMS (Cloud KMS / AWS KMS / HSM).
- Kubernetes cluster(s) host control-plane components (api, frontend, collector, controllers).
- Datastore is managed RDS/Postgres or customer-hosted HA-db; object storage via S3/GCS-compatible endpoint.

Quick glossary:
- cp = control plane (api, console, config-store)
- nodepool = group of VMs for stateless cp pods
- kv-cache = the model-serving in-memory caches (not directly modified here)

Preflight checklist (before any change):
- Access: verify SSH + kubeconfig access; run `kubectl get nodes` and confirm node counts.
- State: `terraform workspace show` and `terraform state list` (sanity spot-check).
- Backups: manual DB snapshot + export tfstate to `state-backups/YYYYMMDD/` in bucket.
- Alerts: notify customer POC and relevant Slack #private-deployments channel.
- Canaries: choose a tiny canary org/tenant to test API after changes.

Initial setup notes (high-level):
1) Networking
   - Ensure at least 3 private subnets for AZ redundancy (or 2 if region constrained).
   - Internal load balancer + health-check path `/healthz`.
   - DNS: internal zone with short TTL for control-plane endpoints; ability to update records quickly for failover.

2) TLS & Trust
   - Use customer PKI where required. For new installs, generate certs via ACME internal CA or customer CA.
   - Cert rotation window: default 48h maintenance window; automate via cert-manager where allowed.

3) Secrets & KMS
   - Terraform state encryption: use backend with customer KMS key.
   - Application secrets stored in Vault or cloud secret manager; ensure KMS IAM roles present.

Terraform module notes (practical tips):
- Module layout: network/, k8s-cluster/, cp-services/, storage/ in repo. Keep cp-services module backwards-compatible: add new resources rather than replace where possible.
- Inputs to watch:
  - `control_plane_version` (semver string) — avoid wildcard for installs; pin during upgrades.
  - `node_pool_sizes` — accept list, default small.
  - `tfstate_backend_bucket` — customer value; ensure lifecycle policy excludes auto-deletion.
- Outputs to consume by other modules: `cp_endpoint`, `cp_ca_fingerprint`, `tfstate_lock_table`.
- State locking: enable dynamodb/gcs lock table to avoid concurrent terraform runs.
- Versioning: tag module releases with `vX.Y.Z` and use module source refs in customer manifests.

Common terraform commands (examples):
- terraform init -backend-config=bucket=redwood-private-state -reconfigure
- terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -out=plan.tfout
- terraform apply "plan.tfout"
- To refresh remote state without changes: `terraform apply -refresh-only` (use with care)

Upgrade plan (control plane minor upgrades):
- Strategy: canary -> staggered rollout -> observe -> full rollout.
- Pre-steps:
  - Create a snapshot of Postgres and copy tfstate backup.
  - Tag current deployment: `kubectl label deployment cp-api roll-tag=pre-upgrade-20250215`
- Canary: update 1 nodepool (lowest-traffic AZ) to new image version; run smoke tests for 1–2 hours.
- Staggered: roll remaining nodepools one at a time, monitor latency and error rate.
- Rollback: have image and helm release artifacts for previous version; `kubectl rollout undo` if >3% error increase sustained >10 minutes.
- Post-upgrade: run regression evals against known prompts (link eval job id in confluence).

Scaling patterns and recommendations:
- Horizontal scaling via nodepools: prefer adding nodes in nodepool over increasing machine size (easier to drain and rotate).
- Autoscaler config:
  - Use cluster-autoscaler with conservative scale-down thresholds (avoid thrashing).
  - Min nodes: set to current baseline; Max nodes: baseline * 3 unless customer capacity limits.
- Pod-level concurrency: tune replica counts for cp-worker and cp-frontend based on p95 latency SLA.
- Cache sizing: if prefix cache pressure increases, add dedicated cache nodepool and set pod anti-affinity.

Evacuation & maintenance run (short-notes for urgent maintenance):
1) Put the control-plane into maintenance mode (if supported) so that new model rollouts are paused.
2) Drain node(s): `kubectl cordon NODENAME && kubectl drain NODENAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3) Monitor pods rescheduling: `kubectl get pods -o wide -w -n redwood-cp`
4) If storage migration needed, coordinate RPO with customer and use `pg_dump` / `pg_restore` for DB; confirm application connections using read-only endpoints first.
5) Rotate minimal secrets after maintenance (see rotation section).

KMS & key rotation (customer controlled):
- Pattern: staggered key creation + alias swap. Never delete old key until all pods restarted and verify decrypted secrets.
- Steps (high-level): create new key, update terraform var pointing at new key alias, apply TF, restart pods that mount secrets, validate.
- Backout: if decryption fails, revert alias (if supported) or restore tfstate and reapply with previous key id.

Certificate rotation (minimal disruption):
- Add new cert to secret, wait for rolling restart or trigger rollout on deployment.
- Health-check all endpoints via internal LB; if any backend fails, fallback to previous cert secret and log the failure.

Example rollback commands:
- kubectl rollout undo deployment/cp-api -n redwood-cp
- terraform apply -var-file=env/prod-rollback.tfvars
- restore db snapshot via RDS console or `pg_restore`

Troubleshooting snippets:
- If terraform plan hangs acquiring lock: check dynamodb/gcs lock table, run `terraform force-unlock` only after ensuring no active runs.
- If pods stuck Pending after scale: check node taints/affinities and available CPU/memory with `kubectl describe pod` and `kubectl describe node`
- High GC pauses after upgrade: revert JVM/Go runtime flags if observed correlation with new image.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on a single canonical tfstate policy for all customers (current practice: customer preference -> fragmentation). Pro: flexibility. Con: operational complexity.
- Explore automated preflight CI job that runs `terraform plan` against a cloned workspace and smoke-tests control-plane API.
- Formalize canary traffic split mechanism (currently manual DNS reroute in many installs).

Postmortem triggers (when to open PD ticket):
- Deployed change that causes >5% increase in 5xx errors for >15min.
- Unrecoverable loss of >1 AZ or nodepool with customer SLA impact.

Notes / historical gotchas (learned):
- TF module refactor in Q3-2024 required state migration that failed for one customer due to non-standard bucket naming — include migration scripts in future PRs.
- Customers with aggressive NAT gateway limits saw pod egress failures during scaling; recommend egress capacity review preinstall.

Appendix: quick checklist for a small upgrade window (1–2 hours)
- 30m prior: backup DB + tfstate snapshot + notify customer.
- 15m prior: create canary tag and deploy to 1 nodepool.
- During: watch error rate, request latency, CPU spikes.
- 15m post-canary: if OK, continue staged rollout.
- After: run regression evals, upload logs to shared bucket, close change with summary in JIRA.

Slack/help channels:
- #private-deployments (ops), #eng-oncall (pager), #release-coord

References:
- See linked PR and Confluence architecture doc for diagrams and detailed module API.

If anything in here is unclear or missing for a specific customer run, ping me (Asha) or @Marco on Slack — keep this doc light and operational.
